title.en: 'Fake gas shortage': Premier's fracking comments draw fury from conservationists
title.zh: “虚假天然气短缺”：州长水力压裂言论引环保人士愤怒

summary.en: Conservationists have criticized the Premier's comments on a gas shortage, arguing that Western Australia's issue is not a lack of supply but rather excessive gas exports.
summary.zh: 环保人士批评州长关于天然气短缺的言论，指出西澳大利亚的问题并非供应不足，而是天然气出口过多。

body.en:
Talk of future gas fracking in a pristine wilderness area to bolster energy supply has sparked fresh fury from conservation groups.

Premier Roger Cook said Western Australia could be forced to permit fracking in the Kimberley region if Woodside Energy's $30 billion offshore Browse project was not developed and the state was left short of gas.

Cook told the Australian Financial Review that WA had a large deficit in its future energy needs, and renewable sources would not be able to replace the gas needed to meet demands from households and heavy industry.

His comments triggered an avalanche of criticism from environmental groups, with about 150 protesters rallying at WA parliament on Friday.

"The WA gas industry has manufactured a fake gas shortage by not supplying their own requisite 15 per cent of domestic gas to the WA market," Greenpeace's Geoff Brice told reporters.

"That is simply not good enough, and they use that to then justify opening up massive new gas expansions in places like the Kimberley and Scott Reef."

The Conservation Council said WA was not facing a gas supply problem, but it did have a gas export problem.

Playing off Woodside's Browse project against fracking in the Kimberley as an either-or scenario was disingenuous and misleading, the council said.

"Gas companies are meant to reserve 15 per cent of their gas for the domestic market, but deliver little more than half of that," executive director Matt Roberts said.

He also raised concerns about the impact Cook's remarks could have on the WA environmental watchdog.

"To have this public pressure mounted and political pressure mounted on the (WA Environmental Protection Authority), I find that unacceptable," he said.

"To think about drilling 50 oil and gas wells around Scott Reef and if that does not happen to frack the Kimberley, we cannot believe that the premier has said this," executive director Martin Pritchard said.

The Chamber of Minerals and Energy said WA would need significantly more gas in the coming years.

"If WA wants to maintain its standard of living ... and Australia wants to be relevant and safe in a more contested world, then it must develop its natural resources," chief executive Aaron Morey said.

"As we've learned through this period of the current global energy crunch, it is our energy resources that have put us in a position to ensure we attract the fuel and other resources we need to stay secure."

The WA domestic gas reservation scheme was a successful policy despite the differences of opinion about how much should be supplied, he said.

The WA Opposition energy spokesperson Steve Thomas said a more pressing issue was the capacity of the Dampier to Bunbury gas pipeline.

title.en: 'Has that been written off?': Fresh questions over Belle Gibson's $410,000 fine
title.zh: “这已经被注销了吗？”：关于 Belle Gibson 410,000 美元罚款的新问题

summary.en: The questions come after Premier Jacinta Allan said the consumer watchdog was "constantly and consistently" pursuing the fine.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Consumer Affairs Victoria has confirmed disgraced wellness influencer Belle Gibson's unpaid $410,000 court penalty has not been written off, with the state consumer watchdog saying it will continue to pursue the debt nearly a decade after the Federal Court ruling.

The clarification came during a parliamentary estimates hearing on Friday, after Victorian Nationals MP Jade Benham questioned officials about the status of the long-outstanding penalty and whether it had effectively been abandoned as bad debt.

Benham referenced comments made by Victorian Premier Jacinta Allan last year that Consumer Affairs Victoria was "constantly and consistently" pursuing Gibson over the fine, imposed in 2017 after she admitted lying about having terminal brain cancer and misleading consumers.

"I don't have any information that says that has been written off," Victoria's Consumer Affairs Minister Paul Edbrooke told the hearing before referring the question to Consumer Affairs Victoria director Nicole Rich.

"Ms Benham, we will continue to pursue that. It's a court penalty, so it will continue to be owed."

A Consumer Affairs Victoria spokesperson told SBS News the watchdog "has continued to undertake actions" to enforce the debt owed by Gibson under court order.

Gibson was ordered by the Federal Court in 2017 to pay $410,000 after Consumer Affairs Victoria successfully sued her for misleading and deceptive conduct over false claims she had terminal brain cancer and other cancers and had cured them through diet and alternative therapies.

She had also falsely claimed profits from her wellness brand, app and cookbook business would be donated to charity.

Interest and penalties later pushed the amount owed beyond $500,000, while authorities previously raided Gibson's Northcote home in attempts to seize assets.

The case returned to public attention last year, following the release of Netflix drama Apple Cider Vinegar, which dramatised Gibson's rise and fall and renewed scrutiny on whether the debt would ever be recovered.

Allan said in February that Consumer Affairs Victoria "won’t let up" in pursuing the outstanding penalty.

body.zh: 维多利亚州消费者事务部已证实，名誉扫地的健康影响者贝尔·吉布森 (Belle Gibson) 未付的 41 万澳元法庭罚款尚未被注销，该州消费者监管机构表示，在联邦法院裁决近十年后，将继续追究这笔债务。 这一澄清是在周五的议会预算听证会上做出的，此前维多利亚州国民议员杰德·贝纳姆 (Jade Benham) 向官员询问了长期未清罚金的状况，以及该罚金是否实际上已被视为坏账而被放弃。 Benham 引用了维多利亚州州长杰辛塔·艾伦 (Jacinta Allan) 去年发表的评论，称维多利亚州消费者事务部正在“持续不断地”追究吉布森的罚款，该罚款是在吉布森承认谎称患有晚期脑癌并误导消费者后于 2017 年处以的。 维多利亚州消费者事务部长保罗·埃德布鲁克（Paul Edbrooke）在听证会上表示：“我没有任何信息表明该费用已被注销，”然后将该问题转交给维多利亚州消费者事务部主任妮可·里奇（Nicole Rich）。 “贝纳姆女士，我们将继续追究这一点。这是法庭的处罚，所以将继续被欠。” 维多利亚州消费者事务部发言人告诉 SBS 新闻，监管机构“继续采取行动”，根据法院命令强制执行吉布森所欠的债务。 2017年，维多利亚州消费者事务部成功起诉吉布森，称她患有晚期脑癌和其他癌症，并通过饮食和替代疗法治愈了这些癌症，该事实具有误导性和欺骗性行为，联邦法院命令吉布森支付41万澳元。 她还谎称其健康品牌、应用程序和食谱业务的利润将捐赠给慈善机构。 后来利息和罚款使所欠金额超过了 50 万美元，而当局此前突击搜查了吉布森在诺斯科特的家，试图没收资产。 去年，Netflix 电视剧《苹果醋》上映后，该案重新受到公众关注，该剧戏剧化地讲述了吉布森的兴衰，并重新审视了债务能否收回的问题。 艾伦二月份表示，维州消费者事务部“不会放松”追究未缴罚款的责任。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

title.en: The 'death tax' debate is back. So what do Australians really pay when they die?
title.zh: 关于“死亡税”的争论又回来了。那么澳大利亚人死后到底要付出什么代价呢？

summary.en: Labor says their trust taxation reforms close trust loopholes. The Opposition says they tax inherited wealth by stealth.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The phrase "death tax" has returned to Australian politics, but whether the government's latest tax changes actually fit that description depends largely on who you ask.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers has repeatedly insisted there are no inheritance taxes or death duties in the federal budget, which was handed down earlier this month.

Chalmers has rejected the Opposition's claim that the proposed reforms to trusts amount to a "death tax", insisting the federal budget will not introduce inheritance taxes or death duties .

Chalmers says deceased estates, fixed trusts and existing testamentary discretionary trusts would all remain exempt under the proposed changes, arguing the government is targeting tax minimisation rather than inherited wealth itself.

The treasurer has also stressed families would still be able to establish fixed testamentary trusts through wills if they want to avoid the proposed minimum 30 per cent tax rate on some discretionary trust structures.

As political backlash intensified following the budget, Chalmers accused opponents of running a "scare campaign" over the reforms, maintaining the government had been transparent about the measures from the outset.

But Opposition leader Angus Taylor disagrees, accusing the government of introducing a "death tax by stealth" through changes to discretionary trusts.

The clash has reignited a politically potent debate Australia has not seriously grappled with in decades: what should happen, tax-wise, when wealth passes from one generation to the next?

Stephen Bartos, economics professor at the University of Canberra, said the reforms cannot be considered an inheritance tax because the proposed changes would only apply to a particular trust tax structure.

"What the changes mean in essence is that in the future, people will not be able to set up a trust in a fashion that allows income splitting and, therefore, allows taxes to be avoided," he said.

"So it doesn't apply retrospectively, it is a change that will apply for the future, and it is to essentially close that loophole," he said.

At the centre of the argument are Labor’s proposed changes to trust taxation.

Under the reforms, some new discretionary trusts would face a minimum 30 per cent tax rate from 2028, reducing the ability for families to distribute trust income to beneficiaries on lower marginal tax rates.

Labor argues the policy is designed to close tax minimisation loopholes disproportionately used by wealthy Australians. body.zh: “死亡税”这个词又回到了澳大利亚政坛，但政府最新的税收改革是否真的符合这个描述，很大程度上取决于你问的是谁。 财政部长吉姆·查尔默斯 (Jim Chalmers) 一再坚称本月早些时候公布的联邦预算中没有遗产税或死亡税。 查尔默斯拒绝了反对派关于拟议的信托改革相当于“死亡税”的说法，坚称联邦预算不会引入遗产税或死亡税。 查默斯表示，根据拟议的改革，已故遗产、固定信托和现有遗嘱全权信托都将保持豁免，他认为政府的目标是税收最小化，而不是继承的财富本身。 财务主管还强调，如果家庭想避免某些全权信托结构拟议的最低 30% 税率，他们仍然可以通过遗嘱建立固定遗嘱信托。 随着预算案出台后政治反弹加剧，查尔默斯指责反对者对改革进行“恐吓运动”，并坚称政府从一开始就对这些措施保持透明。 但反对党领袖安格斯·泰勒不同意，指责政府通过改变全权信托来“秘密征收死亡税”。 这场冲突重新引发了澳大利亚几十年来从未认真应对过的一场具有政治影响力的辩论：当财富从一代人传给下一代时，在税收方面应该发生什么？ 堪培拉大学经济学教授斯蒂芬·巴托斯表示，这项改革不能被视为遗产税，因为拟议的改革仅适用于特定的信托税结构。 “这些变化本质上意味着，在未来，人们将无法以允许收入分割的方式建立信托，从而可以避税，”他说。 他说：“因此，它不会追溯适用，而是适用于未来的变化，而且是从本质上堵住这个漏洞。” 争论的核心是工党提议的信托税改革。 根据改革，一些新的全权信托将从 2028 年起面临最低 30% 的税率，从而降低了家庭以较低边际税率向受益人分配信托收入的能力。 工党辩称，该政策旨在弥补澳大利亚富人过度利用的税收最小化漏洞。政府强调，这些变化不会对遗产或遗产征收直接税，现有的遗嘱信托、已故遗产和固定信托仍将免税。 但反对派关注的是一个不同的论点：一些家庭通过这些继承财富......

title.en: The online threat linked to Australia's worst diphtheria outbreak in decades
title.zh: 与澳大利亚几十年来最严重的白喉疫情相关的网络威胁

summary.en: The disease diphtheria, once nearly eradicated in Australia, has seen a resurgence, with experts attributing its return to underlying societal issues.
summary.zh: 曾几乎在澳大利亚绝迹的白喉病卷土重来，专家们将其复发归因于深层的社会问题。

body.en:
Once one of Australia's most feared childhood diseases, diphtheria killed thousands of children before vaccination programs introduced in the 1930s all but eliminated the infection for decades.

But Australia is now experiencing its largest outbreak since national records began, with more than 230 cases reported in 2026, with the most cases in the Northern Territory.

Cases have also been detected in Queensland, Western Australia and South Australia, while one death in the Northern Territory is believed to have been caused by the disease.

As authorities work to contain the outbreak, health experts say misinformation circulating online risks obscuring the factors actually driving the disease's spread .

Health Minister Mark Butler says there has been a global decline in vaccination rates since the COVID-19 pandemic, alongside growing vaccine hesitancy fuelled in part by misinformation online.

"There is a lingering legacy of vaccine hesitancy that flows from COVID-19 and frankly also from some of the misinformation and disinformation you see online," he told reporters on Thursday.

But Butler also warned it was too early to blame any single cause for the outbreak.

"There are a whole range of social determinants in remote communities that sometimes drive some of these infectious disease outbreaks as well, but I think we need to examine that closely in time," he said.

As the outbreak has grown, false claims about the disease have also begun circulating online.

Some of the misinformation circulating online about the outbreak has falsely linked it to migration.

Associate professor Paul Griffin, director of infectious diseases at the University of Queensland, told SBS News that there is no evidence migrants are responsible for the outbreak, with many cases concentrated in remote Aboriginal communities.

Some posts have suggested the vaccines are more dangerous than the disease itself.

University of Sydney professor Julie Leask, a member of the Sydney Infectious Diseases Institute, told SBS News outbreaks like this often create fertile ground for misinformation, driven by a fear of infectious diseases and xenophobia.

She said social media often allows people to share deeply held beliefs without accountability, particularly in anonymous online spaces.

"When these things come together, people can forensically use infectious diseases as a way of blaming people that they have prejudice against," she said.

"And you even see politicians using this for their political purposes to further division and drive fear around something that can readily be weaponised."

body.zh: 白喉曾经是澳大利亚最令人恐惧的儿童疾病之一，在 20 世纪 30 年代推出的疫苗接种计划几十年来几乎消除了这种感染之前，白喉已导致数千名儿童死亡。 但澳大利亚目前正在经历自有国家记录以来最大规模的疫情爆发，2026 年报告了 230 多例病例，其中北领地病例最多。 昆士兰州、西澳大利亚州和南澳大利亚州也发现了病例，而北领地据信有一人死亡。 在当局努力遏制疫情爆发之际，卫生专家表示，网上传播的错误信息可能会掩盖实际推动疾病传播的因素。 卫生部长马克·巴特勒 (Mark Butler) 表示，自 COVID-19 大流行以来，全球疫苗接种率一直在下降，同时网上错误信息也加剧了人们对疫苗的犹豫不决。 他周四对记者表示：“人们对疫苗犹豫不决，这源于 COVID-19，坦率地说，也源于你在网上看到的一些错误信息和虚假信息。” 但巴特勒也警告说，现在将疫情爆发归咎于任何单一原因还为时过早。 他说：“偏远社区存在一系列社会决定因素，有时也会导致一些传染病的爆发，但我认为我们需要及时仔细研究这一点。” 随着疫情的蔓延，有关该疾病的虚假说法也开始在网上流传。 网上流传的一些有关此次疫情的错误信息错误地将其与移民联系起来。 昆士兰大学传染病主任保罗·格里芬副教授告诉SBS新闻，没有证据表明移民对疫情负责，许多病例集中在偏远的原住民社区。 一些帖子暗示疫苗比疾病本身更危险。 悉尼大学教授、悉尼传染病研究所成员朱莉·莱斯克 (Julie Leask) 告诉 SBS 新闻，由于对传染病的恐惧和仇外心理，此类疫情往往会为错误信息创造肥沃的土壤。 她说，社交媒体通常允​​许人们分享根深蒂固的信念，而无需承担责任，特别是在匿名的在线空间中。 她说：“当这些事情结合在一起时，人们可以在法庭上使用传染病来指责他们有偏见的人。” “你甚至会看到政客利用这一点来达到他们的政治目的，以进一步分裂并引发人们对可以轻易武器化的事物的恐惧。” 格里芬称这些说法“显然是错误的”，并表示疫苗几十年来在控制白喉方面取得的长期成功可能导致一些人低估了……的重要性。
